scope: Static reverse engineering and retrieved sandbox records; no specimen executed locally.

samples.identity: OXI Joiner 1.4.1 encrypted miner/injector bundle with OXI builder decoy
samples.marker: OXI Joiner miner bundle: hidden conhost injector and decoy; add traits
static_evidence: Window callback 0x40110a invokes 0x40135a. Configuration resource 4097 supplies a 16-byte XOR key followed by XOR-encoded records. Resources 1 and 2 contain a compression flag, uncompressed length, and XOR-encoded LZNT1 data. Key recovered from the configuration, not guessed from scan labels.

0x4014bf reads each resource header, 0x4014f4 XOR-decodes it using 0x401a90, 0x401543 calls RtlDecompressBuffer with format 2, and 0x401860 ShellExecuteA launches the path written from that decoded buffer.

Decoded configuration stages fontdrvhost.exe in Temp and launches it with the OXI Joiner application. Both records enable launch and disable the Run-key option. The config disables the outer debugger gate, although both PEB BeingDebugged and NtGlobalFlag branch routines remain present; findings describe static code, not observed anti-debug execution.

Resource 1 expands to a 2,236,928-byte x64 native injector. Its 0x401000 routine decodes buffers with a repeating 32-byte XOR key. Recovered strings include SystemRoot, System32\conhost.exe and executable/argument templates.

Injector 0x4010c4 sleeps four seconds, creates conhost with creation flags 0x08000004, decodes a 2,228,436-byte shellcode buffer, then prepares remote memory and transfers execution through direct syscall wrappers. 0x4014b4 walks ntdll Zw exports and sorts addresses for syscall resolution. No security privilege escalation is inferred.

Resource 2 expands to a UPX-compressed OXI Joiner builder; stock UPX successfully unpacked it and its UI/resources identify the builder. This explains the executable named OXI_Joiner.exe and does not make the companion injector benign.

sandbox_corroboration.details: Retrieved original HTML with forager. Reports user-directory fontdrvhost launch, Defender exclusion modification through PowerShell, scheduled tasks and XMRig in process memory. XMRig identification is sandbox corroboration; the encrypted final mining module was not independently reconstructed here.

samples.coverage_limit: Outer resources are not automatically decoded by atomscan. Three supported suspicious findings cover debugger checks and opaque resource reconstruction; the extracted injector retains its hostile direct-syscall loader finding.

samples.identity: Damaged multi-PE carrier containing UsaShohdi/Shodi host-preserving file-infector code
samples.marker: Shodi-infected PE carrier: host-copy/footer code; detect embedded virus
static_evidence: Outer NSIS-like PE headers describe only 64,512 mapped bytes; its entry point reaches overwritten/mismapped code rather than a coherent NSIS startup path. Multiple PE headers and complete/partial images occur within the body and overlay. Carvings are analysis views, not reconstructed original binaries.

At file offset 0x9a400 lies an 86,016-byte x86 PE with a .ccc section and UsaShohdi marker. Its 0x40123c traverses directories and EXE candidates, excluding Windows/system directories and Norton/IE filenames.

0x401475 copies its own image to a temporary candidate; 0x401a1d renames a host, reads self/host lengths, copies both streams into the output, writes their DWORD lengths and an infection marker, then removes the temporary file. 0x4018ad seeks relative to EOF and reads the paired lengths to identify an existing infection.

Writer at outer file offset 638898 and reader at 637946 use PUSH register/POP ECX transfers instead of the MOV encoding covered by the prior rules. New detection binds their paired-copy context within 2048 bytes.

The last 17 bytes contain lengths (718336, 718336) followed by UsaShohdi. Their total exceeds the actual remaining file length; the first PE header repeats at offset 0xaf600. The file is damaged and successful infection/execution is not asserted.

sandbox_corroboration.details: Retrieved report identifies Shodi by a static signature; both behavioral tasks score 1 and have zero signatures. The collector filename lists unrelated families and is not used as evidence.

samples.coverage_limit: One hostile finding describes the proven file-infection mechanism and one suspicious metadata finding describes the unverified certificate/overlay relation. Additional hostile labels for the same infection would duplicate behavior; no second independent hostile runtime action is established.

samples.identity: Unsigned VMware VMX Helper impostor using encrypted Inno Setup 6.7.0 stages
samples.marker: VMware impostor installer: covert encrypted stages and debugger gates
static_evidence: Version resources claim VMware VMX Helper 3.4.9917.4626, while the manifest/runtime identify Inno Setup. The outer executable has no Authenticode signature; osslsigncode independently confirms that absence.

The installed extractor rejects the revision-2 loader table and new setup format. Built crazy-max/innoextract dev from source fetched with provenance, then extended only the scratch analysis build to retain the 6.5+ outer encryption metadata. Original specimen bytes were never modified.

Extracted actual compiled IFPS bytecode and disassembled it with binary-refinery. InitializeSetup calls IsDebuggerPresent, CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent and NtQueryInformationProcess with classes 7 and 31 and exits on analysis indicators; it also aborts when elapsed probing time exceeds 3000 ms.

_DS implements cyclic string XOR; _GP decodes the bootstrap password from encrypted characters and key Bhpi5Xxl. Its recovered password equals the sandbox /PASSWORD value and successfully decrypts the original installer files.

InitializeSetup relaunches the source image with that password. InitializeWizard places the form at (-32000,-32000), sets dimensions to zero, and calls ShowWindow to hide it. CurStepChanged creates randomized hash-named staging directories, extracts and renames g1_a.exe/g2_c.exe, calls DLL MZ-restoration and 16-byte random append routines, and ShellExec launches the staged programs with -Embedding.

Decryption recovered two x86 native Rust/obfuscated stages, 1,737,632 and 1,708,448 bytes. Both have dense opaque call-pop trampolines. At g1 VA 0x4a7240 GetCurrentProcess supplies the handle passed into WriteProcessMemory at 0x4a728a; GetCurrentProcess also supplies the FlushInstructionCache handle at 0x4a707e. These sites establish local patching, not cross-process injection.

Both extracted stages carry a Take-Two Interactive Software certificate issued in 2011 and expired in 2013. Their stored SHA1 image digests match, but independent osslsigncode trust verification fails and no timestamp is available. This is not VMware provenance; no claim is made that a current trusted signature or stolen private key was established.

sandbox_corroboration.details: Retrieved detailed report shows the password relaunch, randomized Temp launch/update stages, ProgramData Recovery t.exe and SoftwareDistribution Rec.exe, and an RDP port modification. The final remote-access product/family was not independently recovered from the opaque Rust stages.

samples.coverage_limit: Encrypted setup content and its IFPS script are invisible to the installed scanner; automatic extraction emits a setup-data-version gap. The outer file has no supported hostile/suspicious YAML finding. Its new encrypted-files declaration is notable metadata. The manually extracted stages retain suspicious obfuscation. Do not invent two outer hostile rules to meet a count.
samples.judgement_balance: Hidden anti-analysis-gated password relaunch and covert payload launch under false vendor metadata tip the verdict; the sandbox remote-access chain corroborates it. There is no coherent visible VMware installation workflow. No deployment authorization or final operator identity is available.

rule_corrections: Preserve and expand footer-reader/writer matching for equivalent PUSH/POP transfers and executable sections/overlay, keeping original MOV/.text coverage. The new hostile rule requires paired-copy, reader and writer code in proximity, independent of family words, names or metrics.
Move the certificate/overlay structural relation to metadata with identical matcher and severity. Audit ancestor consumers and explicitly preserve their member selection.

Move VMware version-field claims from evasion to version-resource metadata. Bind names to their actual parsed fields, correcting the old false claim that any .rsrc occurrence was the company/description/original filename/product field. The existing masquerade composite remains and references the relocated profile.

Replace the hostile thunk-injection claim with suspicious opaque-thunk plus memory-write/cache API co-occurrence. The previous matcher never required another process or execution transfer; both new stages and the original caa08b42 positive use GetCurrentProcess at the relevant write call. Dense obfuscation remains suspicious. No true injection technique is removed.

The paired-stream copy is a notable file-stream-write observation under micro-behaviors/fs/write/file/stream; the infection composite references it with the EOF reader and footer writer. No generic instruction catalog expansion or inline composite primitive is needed.

positive_fixture_audit.role: Previous native footer writer; preserve recursive-prepender and family findings.
Original thunk-rule positive; inspect local write call at raw offset 0x1c2f00, immediately following GetCurrentProcess at 0x1c2ec3; retain suspicious obfuscation.
Original certificate-carrier positive, re-fetched to check relocation retains the same layout finding.

classifier_disagreement: All three outer ML routes return class 0/BENIGN and calibrated level -1 despite malicious analyst verdicts; the raw probabilities are recorded without using them as behavioral proof. The model reports v18 features versus the v19 extractor. The encrypted Inno/IFPS extraction gap is a concrete remaining miss; OXI final mining behavior also requires manual resource recovery.
validation_engine: /usr/local/var/cyclotron/cleave/target/release/cleave (current source-supported naming budget); installed atomscan embeds an older validator that rejects the documented 101-rule naming exception. Scans used CLEAVE_VALIDATE=0; final explicit make validate uses the current engine.

loss_summary: No supported attack behavior was removed from this batch. VMware field observations and the certificate-overlay relation were relocated. The extracted Rust stages lose one unsupported hostile cross-process-injection label each while retaining suspicious thunk obfuscation and memory-patching API co-occurrence; the historical thunk positive receives the same correction. Broader behavior in the extracted final encrypted payloads remains an extraction gap, not a reason to inflate labels.
coverage_minimum_notes: OXI has three suspicious findings across debugger checks and resource concealment. Shodi has one distinct hostile infection mechanism plus suspicious carrier metadata; extra hostile rules would repeat that mechanism. The VMware impostor outer binary cannot meet the requested hostile/suspicious minimum with supported YAML evidence because its admitted malicious script and payload chain are encrypted and not exposed to this engine. Its recovered script provides multiple independent malicious behaviors, documented above; the extraction/classifier gap is reported instead of making unsupported outer convictions.
